extracted.intended_audience: Saturday Night Live viewers, comedy fans, and general entertainment readers
extracted.subtask_description: A short entertainment-news piece reporting backstage anecdotes about how and when SNL sketches get cut, including performer reactions and where cut sketches may surface. Not a how-to, but it reveals production practices relevant to sketch writers and performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: No sketch is ever fully safe
rubrics_metrics.description: "What you guys don't know is that we have stuff that's cut, like, when we write something on a Tuesday night, it gets cut even before the table read ... We have stuff that goes to dress rehearsal, gets cut after dress rehearsal. We have stuff that gets cut after it goes to the live show."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conveys the production reality that material can be removed at any stage of the pipeline — from initial writing through the live broadcast — so writers and performers should expect fluid selection and last-minute changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of cut points in the production pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Cuts can occur at specific production milestones: during Tuesday writing (even before table read), after the table read, after dress rehearsal, and even during the live show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you're producing or performing sketch material, be aware that approval/retention decisions happen at multiple checkpoints; plan for contingency and quick adjustments at each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate backstage handling when a sketch is cut mid-show
rubrics_metrics.description: "While the live shows happen, they, like, take the wig off of you," she added, "and you're like, 'What's going on?!'" and "someone comes and snatches my wig right off my head."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical and emotional reaction protocol: performers may be abruptly removed from costume/stage; this emphasizes the chaotic, physical, and sometimes jarring nature of mid-show cuts and the need for performers to adapt instantly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared for late-night effort not to air
rubrics_metrics.description: "I had a thing for the finale that we wrote on a Tuesday night 'til 5 am ... that didn't even make the table read," Sherman teased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning to writers/performers that even intensive, last-minute work may not progress; manage expectations and morale accordingly and have alternative material or personal detachment strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional attitude toward cut material
rubrics_metrics.description: "Stuff that got cut, I forgot about anyway," Armisen said, reflecting a tendency to move on from unaired ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry norm/criterion: cultivate resilience and the ability to let go of cut material rather than holding grudges, as a healthy professional approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut sketches as alternative distribution/bonus content
rubrics_metrics.description: "The great thing about sketches that are cut after dress rehearsal: They can often be found online!" and directs readers to watch cut-for-time SNL sketches on Peacock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For writers/performers: even if a sketch is cut from the live show, it may still reach audiences via online platforms (Peacock), so consider secondary distribution when crafting material and understand that cuts don't always mean permanent invisibility.
